In July 1870, France declared war on Prussia expecting a short victorious campaign.

Six weeks later its emperor was a prisoner of war. Ten months later, Germany existed.

The war that built modern Europe — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The spark was almost comically small: a quarrel over whether a Hohenzollern prince could take the vacant Spanish throne. Bismarck edited a telegram from his king — the Ems Dispatch — so it read as an insult, and Paris took the bait.

2/ France expected to fight Prussia alone. Instead the North German Confederation's treaties pulled in Bavaria, Baden, Württemberg and Hesse — the southern states Paris had counted on sitting out. Bismarck got the all-German war he wanted.

3/ The Prussian machine was simply better run. Railways and a professional general staff put several hundred thousand men on the frontier within weeks. French mobilisation was chaos: reservists wandered the country hunting for units already gone.

4/ At Sedan on 1–2 September 1870, an entire French army was encircled and Napoleon III surrendered in person along with roughly 100,000 men. Two days later Paris deposed him and declared a republic — which then fought on for five more months.

5/ Paris was besieged from September to January. Citizens ate the zoo animals; balloons carried mail out over German lines. The city capitulated on 28 January 1871 after bombardment and a winter of starvation.

6/ On 18 January 1871, with Paris still holding out, the German Empire was proclaimed in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles — a German nation-state declared inside the palace of French kings. The venue was chosen deliberately.

7/ The peace took Alsace and much of Lorraine, shown annexed on the last panel, plus five billion francs. In 1919 France chose the same Hall of Mirrors to make Germany sign the Treaty of Versailles.
